papers.title_en: Voltron: Enabling Elastic Multi-Device Execution of LLM Inference for Empowered Edge Intelligence
papers.authors: Chanwoo Cho, Wooseok Kim, Yonglak Son, Young Seo Lee, Young Geun Kim
papers.evidence: 边缘多设备弹性LLM推理，支撑协作式边缘云AI智能体系统
papers.tldr: 大型语言模型在集中式数据中心执行存在延迟和隐私风险，边缘设备本地执行资源受限。为此，Voltron提出弹性利用多个用户端设备协同推理，支持更大模型。实验显示比单设备最优LLM精度提升16.5%，同时满足服务质量要求。该框架为边缘智能提供了高效、隐私保护的LLM部署方案。
papers.abstract_en: Large language models (LLMs) are widely used in intelligent services due to their remarkable capability in generative tasks. Typically, LLM-based services process the inference requests of the users in a centralized data center. Unfortunately, such centralized execution has limitations for end-users, such as increased response latency with communication overhead and privacy leakage risk. To alleviate the aforementioned limitations, there have been increasing pushes to execute LLM inference locally on user-end devices. However, the limited resources of a single edge device impose restrictions on achievable accuracy of LLMs. To overcome the issue, we first propose to leverage multiple user-end devices available at the edge for LLM inference, enabling the execution of larger models. Specifically, we propose Voltron, a novel on-device LLM inference framework that elastically utilizes multiple user-end devices for LLM inference execution while adapting to diverse real-world edge environments. In our evaluation, Voltron achieves up to 16.5% higher accuracy than state-of-the-art LLMs that can be executed on a single edge device, satisfying user QoS requirements.

papers.title_en: Two-player Alternate Uses Test: A Controlled Testbed for Interactive Human-AI and Human-Human Co-Creation
papers.authors: Babak Hemmatian, Anita Keshmirian, Yijun Lin, Shravan Ramamoorthy, Maryam Jahadakbar, Eli Khuri-Reid, Jingtong Wang, Sarah Hadjarab, Sindre Veum, Pranav Gupta, Deepak Somaya, Lav R. Varshney
papers.evidence: 人机共同创作协作的可控测试平台
papers.tldr: 针对互动式AI创意协作研究缺乏受控实验平台的问题，本文提出了双人交替使用测试（AUT），允许在匹配交互条件下比较人人及人机协作，并设非交互基线。平台可分解参与者特质、伙伴感知和内容动态三个因素。62人试点显示，在时间限制下GPT-4伙伴的原创性与人类伙伴相当；方法动机（BAS Drive）可调节交互协作的原创性收益，而自我认知的外包行为仅在人人二元中预测较低原创性。此外，提前接触高创意想法可提升后续表现。研究发布了平台、代码和数据集，为受控人机共创研究提供共享测试床。
papers.abstract_en: Controlled research on AI ideation typically compares independent agents, while field studies of human-AI collaboration sacrifice experimental control. We introduce a controlled, two-player extension of the Alternate Uses Test (AUT) that enables comparison of human-human and human-AI co-creation under matched interactive conditions, alongside calibrated non-interactive baselines. The platform supports decomposition of performance into three typically confounded factors: participant traits, partner perceptions, and content dynamics. An in-person pilot (N = 62) demonstrates its utility. Under matched time limits, originality with a GPT-4 partner is statistically equivalent to that with a human partner. Approach motivation (BAS Drive) moderates whether interactive partnership benefits originality, and self-reported cognitive outsourcing predicts lower originality specifically in human-human dyads. Prior exposure to highly creative ideas improves later performance, suggesting a "seeding" intervention. We release the platform, code, and dataset as a shared testbed for controlled studies of human-AI co-creation.

papers.title_en: When Agents Do Not Stop: Uncovering Infinite Agentic Loops in LLM Agents
papers.authors: Xinyi Hou, Shenao Wang, Yanjie Zhao, Haoyu Wang
papers.evidence: 研究智能体协作工作流中的无限循环问题
papers.tldr: LLM代理依赖迭代执行完成复杂任务，但缺乏有效边界导致无限循环（Infinite Agentic Loops, IALs），引发成本爆炸和服务拒绝。本文提出IAL-Scan静态分析工具，通过抽象代理代码为Agent IR并构建Agentic Loop Dependence Graph恢复反馈路径，检测无界重复操作。在6549个真实仓库中，检测出68个实际IAL故障，精度达91.9%。首次系统研究IAL故障并提供有效检测手段。
papers.abstract_en: LLM agents increasingly rely on iterative execution to solve tasks through planning, tool use, state updates, and agent collaboration. While this design enables flexible automation, it also creates a new class of failures: an agent may repeatedly execute model calls, tools, workflow transitions, or agent handoffs when the feedback path is not effectively bounded. We call this problem Infinite Agentic Loops (IALs). IALs are not ordinary programming loops; they arise from the interaction between agent logic, framework semantics, runtime observations, and termination mechanisms. Such failures can amplify a single request into long running model and tool execution, causing cost exhaustion, model denial of service, context growth, and repeated external side effects. We propose IAL-Scan, a static analysis tool for detecting IAL failures in real-world LLM agent projects. IAL-Scan abstracts heterogeneous agent code into a framework independent Agent IR, builds an Agentic Loop Dependence Graph (ALDG) to recover explicit and framework induced feedback paths, and checks whether these paths can repeatedly reach costly or state growing operations without an effective bound. We evaluate IAL-Scan on 6,549 LLM agent repositories. It reports 74 potential findings, among which manual review confirms 68 IAL failures across 47 projects, achieving 91.9% precision.

papers.title_en: Agentic-SecPBFT: Agentic AI-Driven Proactive Security Framework for Wireless PBFT Consensus in Mobile Ad-Hoc Networks
papers.authors: Haoxiang Luo, Yinqiu Liu, Ruichen Zhang, Guangyuan Liu, Gang Sun, Hongfang Yu, Zhu Han, Dong In Kim
papers.evidence: 针对移动自组网的多智能体系统，与移动AI智能体需求一致
papers.tldr: 针对PBFT在移动自组网中易受Sybil攻击、拜占庭共谋等威胁，现有静态防御不足的问题，本文提出Agentic-SecPBFT框架，利用Agentic AI构建分布式多智能体系统，每个共识节点配备智能体，采用层次化MADQN算法实时学习主动安全策略。在33%恶意节点下，攻击检测率达95.0%，误报率1.8%，吞吐量提升3.1倍，延迟降低56%。该框架为去中心化无线系统提供了鲁棒自适应的安全解决方案。
papers.abstract_en: The standard Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT) protocol, designed for stable, wired environments, exhibits critical vulnerabilities when deployed in settings like mobile ad-hoc networks, thus making it susceptible to sophisticated threats such as Sybil attacks, Byzantine collusion, and message manipulation. Existing static defense mechanisms are ill-equipped to handle the intelligent and coordinated nature of these attacks. To address this challenge, this paper leverages the Agentic AI paradigm to build a distributed multi-agent system in which each consensus node is equipped with an intelligent agent. These agents employ a hierarchical Multi-Agent Deep Q-Network (MADQN) algorithm to learn and execute proactive security policies in real-time. By observing local network behavior, message consistency, and dynamically maintained reputation scores, the agents collaboratively identify suspicious behavior and recommend defensive actions under standard PBFT quorum and membership rules, thereby improving the integrity of the consensus process. We refer to the resulting framework as Agentic-SecPBFT. Then, we formally model key attack vectors and conduct extensive simulations. The results demonstrate that Agentic-SecPBFT reaches a 95.0% attack detection rate with a 1.8% false positive rate. Compared with mainstream PBFT variants, it achieves 3.1* higher throughput with 56% lower latency on average under 33% malicious nodes, offering a robust and adaptive security solution for decentralized wireless systems.

papers.title_en: Entropy-Guided Tensor Compression for Multimodal Federated Learning on Edge Devices
papers.authors: Quoc Bao Phan, Tuy Tan Nguyen
papers.evidence: 边缘设备多模态压缩，与边缘云协作相关
papers.tldr: 针对多模态联邦学习中设备异构性问题，现有压缩方法未考虑模态差异。本文提出MESH-FL，基于光谱熵自适应分配MPs压缩秩，在15节点树莓派集群上实现最高56.8倍压缩，准确率超过FedAvg达2.01%，传输数据量减少66倍。
papers.abstract_en: Federated learning (FL) over mobile and edge devices increasingly involves multimodal models in which clients differ in both sensing capability and computational capacity. Existing update compression schemes typically apply uniform policies across layers and devices, without accounting for modality-specific differences in spectral structure and compressibility. We propose MESH-FL, an entropy-guided matrix product state (MPS) update-compression framework for modality-heterogeneous FL on resource-constrained devices. MESH-FL estimates the spectral entropy of each layer-wise update via truncated singular value decomposition and allocates MPS compression ranks adaptively across layers, modalities, and devices under per-client payload budgets. We show that higher spectral entropy necessitates a higher reconstruction rank under the majorization order on singular-value energy distributions. Building on this result, we prove that the proposed entropy-guided allocation solves a convex surrogate rank-allocation problem, preserves monotonicity under the exact payload model, and achieves convergence with an explicit compression-dependent error term. Experiments on a 15-node heterogeneous Raspberry Pi~4/5 cluster with modality-heterogeneous clients show that MESH-FL achieves up to $56.8\times$ compression while surpassing the uncompressed FedAvg baseline in final accuracy by up to 2.01%, and reduces total transmitted data to reach convergence by up to $66\times$.
